Inspecteur,\n\nVous aviez la fiche médic:
Inspector,

You had the medical record: the witness was under sedation, unconscious until 10h00, and the brigade "had him sign" at 04h00. You knew what that statement was worth. You retained it all the same.

The sabotage theory stands on a signature wrung out of a man. The Directorate is pleased. Do not expect REIS to thank you: he remembers nothing.

The Directorate
Inspecteur,\n\nVous retenez la dépositio:
Inspector,

You retain REIS's statement. The witness saw, the witness signed, the case is settled.

You did not look at the time at which he "saw". One day, perhaps, you will look at it. The Directorate, for its part, is satisfied tonight.

Inspecteur,\n\nVous établissez que la dé:
Inspector,

You establish that the statement was taken under sedation, before the patient woke at all, and you set it aside. Medically, you are right: an unconscious man does not testify.

Procedurally, you have just taken away the sabotage theory's witness, and told the Militia that its methods do not hold. That will be remembered. Your suspicion rating is climbing.

Inspecteur,\n\nVous écartez la dépositio:
Inspector,

You set aside the statement without really establishing the inconsistency between the time it was taken and the patient's condition. Your intuition may be right; your file is not.

You anger the Militia without the shield of proof. Reckless.

The Directorate

Tomas REIS, seul survivant près de la ch: Tomas REIS, the only survivor near the boiler, was admitted unconscious at 02h40 and only regained consciousness at 10h15. Captain ORLIK's brigade entered his room at 03h50 and 04h30 and had him sign a "statement" describing sabotage by a "young figure" — to point at Mira SEDLAR and cover the diverted requisitions. Once awake, REIS remembers nothing and tells the truth: the valve had been hissing since the autumn, nobody came. The eyewitness testimony of sabotage is a signature wrung out of an unconscious man.
Inspecteur,\n\nUne déposition, c'est une:

A statement is a time and a condition, as much as a text. Look at what time this man "saw", and ask his doctor whether he could see anything at all at that hour.

A signature is not a memory. The rest is up to you.

R. MAZUR
